# Willrun

> Willrun answers whether a specific portable power station or generator can run a specific appliance, using published running and starting watts, an 85% inverter allowance for stations, and 30 amp inlet math for home backup.

Willrun is a static site. Every station and appliance row cites a manufacturer or ENERGY STAR URL. Runtime is nameplate watt-hours times 0.85, divided by average draw. The calculator, outage planners, brand comparison, CPAP/BiPAP pages, station and appliance runtime tables, and every station-and-appliance answer page (alongside the simple estimate) also add about 15 W of inverter self-consumption (the figure BLUETTI uses for its AC180) to the draw: Wh × 0.85 ÷ (W + 15). CPAP pages show DC-converter nights separately as a best case. Verdicts are runs, runs with surge risk, won't run, or no run verdict when running watts were not published.

## Start here
- [Calculator](https://willitrunpower.com/): pick a station, add appliances, read the verdict.
- [Methodology](https://willitrunpower.com/methodology/): the 0.85 allowance, duty cycle, and how surge is treated.
- [Stations](https://willitrunpower.com/stations/): 24 models.
- [Appliances](https://willitrunpower.com/appliances/): 51 loads.
- [Affiliate disclosure](https://willitrunpower.com/disclosure/)
- [About Willrun](https://willitrunpower.com/about/): who publishes the site (EYEVUE Ventures), how the numbers are made, contact eyevueventures@gmail.com.
- [Privacy policy](https://willitrunpower.com/privacy/): cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics, no accounts; an optional real-world test submission form (data + proof photo/link stored in Cloudflare, email optional and never published), affiliate cookies set only on the retailer's site, no sale of data. Effective 2026-10-27.
- [Submit a real-world test](https://willitrunpower.com/submit-test/): readers send measured appliance/CPAP watts or runtime on a power station with a photo or proof link. Every entry is reviewed by hand; verified results are published as "Verified owner test" data.

## Guides
- [All guides (hub)](https://willitrunpower.com/guides/): index of generator sizing, generator vs power station, quiet generators, brand comparison and best-station-by-job guides.
- [Best power station for the job (hub)](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/): fridge, CPAP, camping, RV, home backup and sump pump guides, with the deciding spec for each job.
- [Best power station under $500 (2026)](https://willitrunpower.com/guides/best-power-station-under-500/): buying guide by decision. Maker prices 2026-10-24: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 $499 (1,070 Wh, 3,000 W surge, <20 ms UPS, 23.8 lb), Anker SOLIX C1000 $469.99 sale (1,056 Wh, 2,400 W surge, 600 W solar, expands to 2,112 Wh), EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus $299 (286 Wh, <10 ms UPS), RIVER 2 Pro $389 (768 Wh, X-Boost not a motor rating), BLUETTI AC180 $499 and AC70 $359 out of stock. Only published motor surge >=1,200 W counts for a fridge; runtimes use Wh x 0.85 / (load + 15 W).
- [EcoFlow vs Jackery vs BLUETTI: which one should you buy?](https://willitrunpower.com/guides/ecoflow-vs-jackery-vs-bluetti/): brand comparison by decision (budget and $/Wh, outage length with ~15 W inverter draw, CPAP/UPS switchover, solar input, warranty fine print, app and expansion) with maker prices checked 2026-10-21. EcoFlow: fastest published UPS (<10 ms DELTA 3 Plus / RIVER 3 Plus), most solar and expansion. Jackery: lightest per kWh (1000 v2 23.8 lb, 2000 v2 39.5 lb), but 400 W solar and no expansion on v2, warranty 3+2 only via authorized sellers. BLUETTI: AC180 cheapest per Wh ($0.43, out of stock to late Nov), AC200L $899 with 1,200 W solar, 7,200 W surge, 8,192 Wh expansion.
- [Best power station for a refrigerator in a power outage](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/fridge/): ENERGY STAR median use by fridge type (top-freezer 363 kWh/yr, bottom-freezer 538, side-by-side 640, door-ice French door 715), a 1,200 W motor-start surge rule (Haier 805 W start-up; Champion 800–1,200 W), runtimes on 13 stations, capacity needed for 12 h to 3 days, and solar panel watts by state vs each station's solar input limit.
- [Power station for an oxygen concentrator](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/oxygen-concentrator/): maker wattages (Philips EverFlo 350 W avg, Invacare Perfecto2 V 325 W typical, DeVilbiss 525DS 310 W avg / 275 W at <=2.5 L/min, Inogen At Home 275 W max / ~100 W at setting 2); hours = Wh x 0.85 / (W + 15): 1 kWh station ~2.5-3.1 h at 275-350 W, ~7.9 h at 100 W; 8 h at 350 W needs ~3,435 Wh. Picks: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (bridge), Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus (overnight at ~100 W), EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (overnight at 300-350 W). Inogen One G5 DC input 13.5-15.0 V vs 12 V station car ports. Medical: keep supplier backup cylinders; ALA says do not lower flow without your doctor.
- [Power station for an insulin fridge](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/insulin-fridge/): FDA: insulin in maker vials/cartridges may stay unrefrigerated at 59-86F for up to 28 days; fridge 36-46F; never freeze; pump insulin out if >98.6F. Dometic CFX3 25 0.92 Ah/h at 12 V (~11 W, 90F room) on car port: hours = Wh x 0.85 / 11.04 (1,070 Wh ~82 h; 768 Wh ~59 h; 2,043 Wh ~157 h). Danby compact fridge on AC 24.9-27.5 W avg + 15 W inverter: 1,070 Wh ~21-23 h. Day need: cooler ~312 Wh, compact fridge ~1,127-1,200 Wh. FRIO wallet 64-79F 45 h at 100F (in-use only). Not medical advice.
- [Best power station for a CPAP](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap/): Buying guide by decision: humidifier vs heated tube (ResMed AirSense 11: 7 W off, 19 W humidifier, 55 W heated tube), DC converter vs AC (inverter idle draw about 15 W per BLUETTI, so AC humidifier-off nights are far lower than capacity ÷ watts), nights needed, UPS switchover times (DELTA 3 Plus and RIVER 3 Plus <10 ms; Jackery 1000 v2/2000 v2 and Anker C1000 <20 ms; RIVER 2 Pro <30 ms), ResMed Air11/Air10 DC converter current limits, auto-off timers, FAA 100 Wh flight limit, and maker medical-use caveats. Picks: DELTA 3 Plus, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, BLUETTI AC180, RIVER 2 Pro, RIVER 3 Plus, Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, DELTA 2 Max.
- [Best power station for camping](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/camping/): For a carried campsite, the EcoFlow RIVER 2 (7.7 lb, 256 Wh) and Anker SOLIX C300 (288 Wh) cover a CPAP and lights; a Danby compact fridge pushes you toward the RIVER 2 Pro, DELTA 2, or AC180 if you can spare the weight.
- [Best power station for an RV](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/rv/): 13.5K BTU roof AC ~15 A / 1,800 W hot-day (Micro-Air), 15K ~1,944 W; hours = Wh x 0.85 / (W+15): DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh, TT-30R+L14-30R) 1.9 h nonstop, F3800 (14-50) 1.8 h, 2 kWh TT-30 stations (AC200L, F2000) ~1.0 h. Penguin II LRA 63 A + fan 8.5 A (~8,580 W on paper), Dometic 3.5 kW min generator; soft starter (EasyStart: 13.5K starts on 2,000 W generator) recommended. TT-30 on a 2,400 W station is not a 3,600 W 30 A service; RV converter (PD4655 up to 950 W input) drains the station - switch it off. Absorption fridge electric element 325 W - use propane. Suburban SF-30 furnace 6.5 A at 12 V, Shurflo 4008 7.5 A max, MaxxFan 2.5 A high. Example boondock day ~743 Wh at devices, ~1,500 Wh from station via shore cord + converter + 24 h inverter.
- [Best power station for home backup](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/home-backup/): On stored energy alone, the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096 Wh) outlasts the Anker SOLIX F3800 (3,840 Wh), while the F3800 has the higher continuous output at 6,000 W. A 1,500 W Lasko heater needs at least 1,500 W continuous or a documented resistive boost.
- [Best power station for a sump pump](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/sump-pump/): The Zoeller Model 53 at 115 V draws 1,115.5 W while running. Stations under that — including the RIVER 2 series, the AC70, and the Yeti 500X — will not hold it. Stations above it still carry a surge risk because Zoeller does not publish starting amps.

## CPAP and BiPAP
Watt figures come from ResMed's published therapy-device power table and the Philips DreamStation humidifier manual (80 W supply, used as a worst case). Medical pages carry a safety notice: estimates only, confirm approved power sources with the manufacturer and your supplier.
- [CPAP and BiPAP on battery power: every model and setting](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap/): A CPAP night costs anywhere from about 50 Wh to more than 500 Wh. The humidifier and heated tube decide the size of power station you need, not the machine. Tables show AC nights (including about 15 W of inverter draw) and DC-converter nights separately; e.g. an AirSense 11 with no humidifier gets about 4.9 nights on a 1,024 Wh station on AC versus up to 15.5 on DC.
- [Best power station for a CPAP](https://willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap/): Buying guide with picks by situation (bedside UPS, camping on DC, budget, multi-night heated humidity) and runtimes that include about 15 W of inverter idle draw on AC.
- [CPAP during a power outage: how long each setup lasts](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-during-power-outage/): Turn the humidifier and heated tube off during an outage if your doctor agrees. On ResMed's figures that cuts nightly use from about 440 Wh to about 56 Wh.
- [CPAP camping: how to power a CPAP with no electricity](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-camping/): For camping, turn humidity off and use the DC cord if your machine has one. An AirSense 11 then needs about 56 Wh a night, so a 256 Wh station covers about four nights.
- [How many watts does a CPAP use? Every ResMed setting](https://willitrunpower.com/how-many-watts-does-a-cpap-use/): ResMed measures its CPAPs at 6.3 to 7 W without a humidifier, 19 to 22 W with a humidifier, and 34 to 55 W with a heated tube.
- [BiPAP battery backup: ResMed AirCurve runtimes](https://willitrunpower.com/bipap-battery-backup/): A ResMed AirCurve BiPAP uses 8 to 9 W without a humidifier and up to 66 W with a humidifier and heated tube, close to a CPAP.
- [CPAP on DC vs AC: which lasts longer on a power station?](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-dc-vs-ac-power-station/): Running a CPAP from a power station's 12 V port with the maker's DC cord skips the station's inverter, so it usually lasts longer than the AC estimates on this site. With the humidifier off the gap is about 3x, because the inverter's own ~15 W draw is more than the CPAP's.
- [Can a car battery run a CPAP? The real math](https://willitrunpower.com/can-a-car-battery-run-a-cpap/): A typical 12 V car battery can run a CPAP without humidity for a night, but deep discharges damage car batteries, and Philips warns against running its machines while the engine is running.
- [What size solar panel do you need for a CPAP?](https://willitrunpower.com/cpap-solar-panel-size/): To refill one CPAP night from the sun, divide the nightly watt-hours by your sun hours and allow for loss. Without humidity on a DC cord, a 50 W panel is plenty (about 60 W if the CPAP runs on AC); with a heated tube, plan on about 150 W, or 190 W on AC.
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 11 with HumidAir 11 humidifier, no heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-11-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 AutoSet with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirSense 10 with HumidAir and ClimateLineAir heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-airsense-10-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 10 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir and heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-10-vauto-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP, no humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto-no-humidifier/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir humidifier?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto/)
- [Will a power station run ResMed AirCurve 11 VAuto BiPAP with HumidAir and heated tube?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/resmed-aircurve-11-vauto-heated-tube/)
- [Will a power station run Philips DreamStation, worst case at the 80 W power supply rating?](https://willitrunpower.com/appliance/philips-dreamstation-max-rated/)

## Outages
- [24-hour outage](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/24-hour/): only the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and Anker SOLIX F3800 cover this 24-hour mix once about 15 W of inverter self-consumption is counted (1,608 Wh of appliances + 360 Wh idle = 1,968 Wh, about 2,315 Wh nameplate); the 2 kWh class is about 230 Wh short.
- [3-day power outage backup plan](https://willitrunpower.com/outage/3-day/): A 3-day outage with a full-size fridge, CPAP, router, laptop and lights takes about 6,666 Wh including ~15 W inverter draw (about 7,840 Wh nameplate). Compares battery-only expandable systems (DELTA Pro 3, F3800 Plus, AC200L, Jackery 2000 Plus, DELTA 2 Max), solar with PVWatts monthly sun hours for six cities, and a generator-recharged battery (~1.4 gal over 3 days vs ~8.4 gal running an EU2200i 24/7). CDC CO and FoodSafety.gov guidance, medical note.

- [Generator vs power station](https://willitrunpower.com/guides/generator-vs-power-station/)
